description: Per (drug, event) biological plausibility ratings. Key format: '{drug_canonical}::{event_meddra_pt}' — lowercase canonical drug name from chembl_lookup.json, MedDRA Preferred Term in snake_case.
source_policy: HUMAN_CURATED — rubric defined in prompts/evidence_grading_rubric.txt. Entries must include ChEMBL ID reference and written rationale.

semaglutide::pancreatitis.rationale: GLP-1 receptor agonism directly stimulates pancreatic exocrine secretion and has been shown in preclinical models to increase pancreatic ductal pressure. Several mechanistic reviews support a biological link.

metformin::lactic_acidosis.rationale: Metformin inhibits mitochondrial complex I, impairing lactate oxidation in hepatocytes. In patients with renal impairment, accumulation leads to elevated lactate levels. Well-established pharmacological mechanism.

atorvastatin::common_cold.rationale: HMG-CoA reductase inhibition has no established mechanistic pathway affecting rhinovirus susceptibility or upper respiratory tract immune response. This pair is a negative-control entry.

montelukast::suicidal_ideation.rationale: CysLT1 receptors are primarily targeted in the peripheral airways. While leukotrienes may have some role in neuroinflammation, direct causal mechanisms linking antagonism to suicidal ideation are not well established pharmacologically.

ciprofloxacin::tendon_rupture.rationale: While primarily targeting bacterial DNA gyrase and Topoisomerase IV, fluoroquinolones are known to exert off-target toxic effects on mammalian cells, potentially altering collagen synthesis and upregulating matrix metalloproteinases in tendocytes.

pembrolizumab::pneumonitis.rationale: PD-1 inhibition directly removes negative regulation of T-cell activation. This mechanism of unleashing systemic immune responses inherently carries a high biological plausibility for autoimmune and inflammatory toxicities, including pneumonitis.

liraglutide::pancreatic_cancer.rationale: GLP-1 receptor agonism stimulates pancreatic exocrine and endocrine function. While chronic hyperstimulation theoretically provides a plausible pathway to hyperplasia or neoplasia, the direct link to carcinogenesis is complex and indirect.

atorvastatin::dementia.rationale: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors block cholesterol synthesis. Since brain cholesterol (synthesized locally) is critical for neuronal function and myelin maintenance, statins that cross the blood-brain barrier could plausibly impair cognition, though dementia is a chronic complex process.

albuterol::suicidal_ideation.rationale: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonism causes sympathetic activation (tachycardia, tremor), but there is no direct established pharmacological mechanism linking peripheral or central beta-2 stimulation to complex psychiatric events like suicidal ideation.
